verdict.rationale: Community evidence shows the source can be read and modified: one user says the Elastic License option lets them self-host, fix bugs and add features, and compares it with AGPL, which hints that an AGPL option now exists. Other community items describe the core as 'formerly-OSS', note SSPL failing a company's open-source policy, and call X-Pack security not open source, so the license's openness is contested. Missing for 10: any first-party documentation of the license or a public source repository, explicit confirmation of an OSI-approved license (e.g. AGPL) for the core, and clarity on which components are open versus proprietary.
